subject: [PATCH 1/2] crypto: zstd - use vmalloc() for stream workspaces

reviews.author: Rik van Riel
reviews.summary: Rik quickly acknowledged the patch as a good catch, indicating that he agrees with the proposed change to use vmalloc() instead of kvmalloc(). He also added his Reviewed-by tag.

2026-11-11.patch_summary: This patch series aims to optimize memory allocation for zstd compression streams by switching from kvmalloc() to vmalloc(). The change is motivated by the fact that vmalloc() can reduce memory usage in certain scenarios, specifically when allocating large blocks of memory. The patch modifies the zstd_alloc_stream() function to use vmalloc() instead of kvmalloc(), and also updates the corresponding free function to use vfree().

reviews.author: Johannes Weiner
reviews.summary: Johannes also agreed with the patch, stating that there isn't enough turnover to justify the kmalloc optimization. He added his Reviewed-by tag.
reviews.raw_body:
On Wed, Nov 11, 2026 at 07:07:39AM -0800, Usama Arif wrote:
> The zstd acomp streams retain their workspaces after the last transform
> has been freed. The first is allocated during transform initialization;
> additional per-CPU streams are allocated on demand. They are released
> when the algorithm is unregistered.
> 
> In a 4 KiB-page x86-64 build, each stream requests 1,566,281 bytes.
> If kvmalloc() succeeds via kmalloc(), it occupies an order-9 block
> (2 MiB). vmalloc() needs 383 backing pages (1,532 KiB), 516 KiB fewer
> per stream. Across 384 populated streams, that is 193.5 MiB less
> workspace backing if all would have used kmalloc(). There is no such
> gain when kvmalloc() already falls back to vmalloc().
> 
> Use vmalloc() and vfree() directly to avoid the high-order allocation.
> This uses vmalloc address space, page tables and bookkeeping; the
> figures above compare workspace backing only.
> 
> Signed-off-by: Usama Arif <usama.arif@linux.dev>

Nice catch. Given the lifetime of these streams, there really isn't
enough turnover to justify the kmalloc optimization to begin with.

Reviewed-by: Johannes Weiner <hannes@cmpxchg.org>

reviews.author: Chris Down
reviews.summary: Chris pointed out that vmalloc() doesn't avoid high-order allocations as previously thought, but instead asks for an order-8 block first and then splits it up. He suggested rephrasing the patch to focus on avoiding kmalloc() rounding up to a 2 MiB block.
reviews.raw_body:
Hi Usama,

Usama Arif writes:
>Use vmalloc() and vfree() directly to avoid the high-order allocation.

vmalloc() doesn't avoid high-order allocations any more. Since
a06157804399 ("mm/vmalloc: request large order pages from buddy
allocator"), vm_area_alloc_pages() first tries the largest order that
fits, and splits the block up afterwards. So for these 383 pages it still
asks for an order-8 block first, then order 6, 5, 4, 3, 2 and 1.

What the patch does avoid is kmalloc() rounding the 1.5 MiB up to a 2 MiB
block, which is where the 516 KiB per stream comes from. Maybe say that
instead?

Once that's fixed, please feel free to add:

Reviewed-by: Chris Down <chris@chrisdown.name>
Tested-by: Chris Down <chris@chrisdown.name>

Chris
